label: Sinus rhythms
blurb: The sinoatrial node is in charge: every QRS is preceded by a P wave with a constant PR interval. Only the rate differs.

label: Atrial arrhythmias
blurb: The atria depolarise from somewhere other than the sinus node — chaotically in fibrillation, as a single re-entrant circuit in flutter.

label: Supraventricular tachycardias
blurb: A fast, regular, narrow-complex rhythm arising at or above the atrioventricular node, usually by re-entry.

label: Ventricular arrhythmias
blurb: Depolarisation begins in ventricular myocardium and spreads cell to cell, so the QRS is broad. These are the peri-arrest rhythms.

label: Atrioventricular block
blurb: Conduction from atria to ventricles is delayed, intermittently interrupted, or completely absent — read the P waves against the QRS complexes.

label: Intraventricular conduction
blurb: The atrioventricular node conducts normally, but one bundle branch does not: the ventricles are activated in sequence rather than together, so the QRS is broad and repolarisation follows it.

label: Chamber enlargement
blurb: More myocardium generates a larger vector. Voltage criteria are supportive, not diagnostic — the echocardiogram measures the muscle.

label: Ischaemia & injury
blurb: The ST segment and T wave report the state of the myocardium: acute injury, evolving infarction and pericardial inflammation each have a signature.

label: Metabolic & electrolyte
blurb: Potassium sets the resting membrane potential, so it rewrites repolarisation on the surface ECG before it stops the heart.
